v.why: Replacing a skip_connect on edge 0 with a 3x3 conv gave +43 on C10 and +17 on IN16 in the all-skip parent, versus roughly zero elsewhere.
Replacing a pooling edge with a conv adds learnable capacity, giving +43 in the all-pool parent and clear gains in the mixed parent.
Upgrading the final skip edge to a conv gave +45 on C10 and C100 and +17.5 on IN16, versus small changes when edge 5 was already a conv.
Removing a skip on edge 5 in the all-skip parent gave +42 on C10, whereas removing a conv edge 5 gave negative changes.
Deleting a 3x3 conv on edge 4 hurt in every such parent (as much as -77 on C10), whereas deleting a pool or skip on edge 4 helped or was neutral.
Dropping a pooling edge in the all-pool parent gave +15 and +17 on C10 and C100, while dropping conv edges gave losses.
Adding a 3x3 conv where the direct edge was absent gave large gains, especially on IN16 (+17 to +19), versus negative changes when edge 3 was a skip.
Replacing a pooling edge 3 with a conv gave +37.6 on C10 in the all-pool parent, versus near-zero or negative changes in conv-rich parents.
Upgrading a skip edge 4 to a conv gave +35 on C10 and +33 on C100 in the all-skip parent, versus about zero when edge 4 was already a conv or none.
Restoring a skip path where edge 3 was none helped consistently, +3 to +22 on IN16, whereas replacing existing pool or conv edges was neutral or harmful.

raw:

These gave gains of up to +45 points when the replaced edge was skip_connect or avg_pool, against small or negative changes elsewhere. The weakest is the last one (edge 3 -> skip_connect when edge 3 is none), where the effect is moderate and the comparison cases are few.
